notes.summary: Non-verbal questions use pictures instead of words. The common ones are mirror and water images, folding a paper and punching or cutting it, folding a transparent sheet, and counting triangles or squares in a figure. Each has a fixed rule: a mirror swaps left and right, water swaps top and bottom, each fold doubles the holes, and counting is done in a fixed order so nothing is missed.

concepts.title: Mirror image
concepts.body:
A mirror placed beside a figure (on its left or right, a vertical line) swaps left and right. Top and bottom stay the same.
  • The order of letters reverses and each letter flips: "CGL" reads as a backwards L, G, C.
  • Letters that look the same in such a mirror: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y. Numbers: 0 and 8.
  • A mirror on the left or on the right gives the same image; only the line's direction matters.
  • If the mirror line is horizontal (above or below), the image is the same as a water image.

concepts.title: Water image
concepts.body:
Water below an object reflects it upside down: top and bottom swap, left and right stay the same.
  • The order of letters does not change; each letter turns upside down.
  • Letters that look the same in water: B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X. Numbers: 0, 3 and 8.
  • Mirror image followed by water image equals a half-turn (180° rotation).

concepts.title: Checking options quickly
concepts.body: Do not redraw the whole figure. Pick one or two asymmetric details (a small dot, an arrow tip, the letter F or the number 4) and check where they go. Options that rotate the figure, reflect it the wrong way, or only reverse the order without flipping each character are the usual distractors.

concepts.title: Paper folding and punching
concepts.body:
Every fold doubles the number of layers, so a hole punched through all layers appears 2, 4 or 8 times when unfolded.
  1. Unfold in reverse order: undo the last fold first.
  2. At each step, reflect every hole across that fold line.
  3. A hole punched exactly on a fold line is not doubled by that fold.

In the figure: fold left onto right, then top onto bottom, then punch once. Undoing fold 2 adds a hole reflected across the horizontal line; undoing fold 1 copies both to the left. Result: 4 holes in a symmetric pattern.

concepts.title: Cutting on a fold
concepts.body: A cut on the folded edge opens out into a shape that is symmetric about the fold line. Half a triangle cut on the fold becomes a full diamond; half a circle becomes a full circle. A cut away from the fold appears twice, mirror-wise. Diagonal folds work the same way: reflect across the diagonal.

concepts.title: Folding a transparent sheet
concepts.body:
On a transparent sheet you can see every mark after folding. The half that does not move keeps its marks as they are; the half that is folded over lands on top, reflected across the fold line. The folded sheet shows both sets together.

In the figure: the triangle on the left half pointed right; after folding it lands on the right half pointing left, next to the circle that was already there.

concepts.title: Counting triangles
concepts.body:
Count in a fixed order so nothing is missed: single small triangles first, then triangles made of 2 parts, then 3, and so on. Labelling the corners with letters helps.
  • Square with both diagonals: 8 triangles.
  • n lines from one corner (the sides included) meeting a single base: n(n − 1)/2 triangles.
  • The same fan crossed by k lines parallel to the base: k × n(n − 1)/2.

In the figure: 4 lines from the top corner and 2 horizontal lines, so 2 × (4 × 3 ÷ 2) = 12 triangles.

concepts.title: Counting squares and rectangles
concepts.body:
• Squares in an n × n grid: 1² + 2² + … + n² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6. A 3 × 3 grid has 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.
  • Rectangles (squares included) in an m × n grid: choose 2 of the m + 1 vertical lines and 2 of the n + 1 horizontal lines: C(m + 1, 2) × C(n + 1, 2). A 3 × 3 grid has 6 × 6 = 36.
  • For odd figures, count by size: smallest shapes first, then those made of 2, 3, 4 parts.
  • Read the question: "squares (rectangles not included)" means only equal-sided shapes.

varieties.name: Mirror image
varieties.how: A side mirror swaps left and right only: reverse the order and flip each character sideways; top and bottom stay.

example.q: Select the mirror image of "CGL 2025" when a mirror is placed on its right.
steps: Left and right swap, so the order becomes 5, 2, 0, 2, space, L, G, C.
Each character is also flipped sideways: the 2s and 5 face the other way, and L has its foot pointing left.
Top and bottom do not change, so nothing is upside down.
example.answer: The right-hand picture in the figure

varieties.name: Water image
varieties.how: Water swaps top and bottom only: keep the order, turn each character upside down.

steps: The order stays C, G, L, 2, 0, 2, 5 from left to right.
Each character is turned upside down: L has its foot at the top, C still opens to the right.
Nothing is reversed left to right.
example.answer: The lower picture in the figure

varieties.name: Paper folding, punching and cutting
varieties.how: Unfold in reverse order, reflecting every hole or cut across each fold line. Holes double with each fold.

example.q: A square sheet is folded left onto right, then top onto bottom, and one hole is punched as shown. How will it look when unfolded?
steps: Two folds make 4 layers, so expect 4 holes.
Undo fold 2 (horizontal): the hole near the middle line gets a partner just above that line.
Undo fold 1 (vertical): both holes get partners on the left half.
example.answer: Four holes, two on each side, in a square around the centre

varieties.name: Folding a transparent sheet
varieties.how: Keep the fixed half as it is; reflect the moving half across the fold line and lay it on top.

example.q: A transparent sheet has a triangle on its left half and a circle on its right half. It is folded left onto right along the dotted line. How does it look?
steps: The right half does not move, so the circle stays at its place.
The left half flips over the dotted line, so the triangle moves to the right half and now points the other way.
Both marks show through the transparent sheet.
example.answer: A half-width sheet with the circle and the reversed triangle

varieties.name: Counting triangles
varieties.how: Count small triangles first, then bigger ones made of 2, 3 or more parts; use the fan formula when lines meet at one corner.

example.q: How many triangles are there in the figure?
steps: 4 lines start at the top corner (2 sides and 2 inside lines).
Any 2 of them with one horizontal line make a triangle: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6 for each horizontal line.

varieties.name: Counting squares, rectangles and other shapes
varieties.how: Count by size: 1 × 1 squares, then 2 × 2, then 3 × 3. For an n × n grid the total is 1² + 2² + … + n².

example.q: How many squares are there in the 3 × 3 grid?

tips: Mirror (side): left and right swap. Water: top and bottom swap.
Track one odd detail (a dot, an arrow tip, the letter F) instead of the whole figure.
Each fold doubles the holes; unfold the last fold first.
A cut on a fold opens into a shape symmetric about the fold line.
Count shapes by size, smallest first, and write the running total.
Squares in an n × n grid: n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6.
traps: Reversing only the order of letters without flipping each one is a common wrong option.
A water image is not the same as a 180° rotation; the left-right order stays the same.
A hole punched on a fold line is not doubled by that fold.
In triangle counting, do not miss the big triangles formed by combining several small ones.
"Squares" questions sometimes say rectangles are not included; read the brackets.

questions.q: Select the correct mirror image of the given figure when the mirror is placed at MN as shown.
questions.solution:
A mirror on the right side (vertical line MN) swaps left and right only; top and bottom stay the same.
So "REASON 47" appears in reverse order with every character flipped left to right, still upright: option (b).
(a) is a 180° turn (upside down), (c) only reverses the order without flipping, (d) is the water image.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure (a square with both diagonals)?
questions.solution:
Small triangles formed at the centre: 4.
Triangles made of two small ones (half of the square cut by one diagonal): ABC, BCD, CDA, DAB = 4.
Total = 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.q: Select the correct water image of the given figure (MN is the water surface).
questions.solution:
Water image: top and bottom swap, left and right stay the same.
The flag (top-left) moves to the bottom-left, the circle (bottom-right) moves to the top-right, and the flag still points right: option (d).
(a) is the mirror image, (b) is a 180° rotation, (c) is a 90° rotation.

questions.q: A square sheet of paper is folded along the dotted line (left half onto the right half) and then a hole is punched as shown. How will the sheet look when unfolded?
questions.solution:
The fold line is vertical, in the middle.
The hole is in the upper part of the folded sheet, near the top.
On unfolding, it gets a partner reflected across the middle line at the same height.
So there are two holes at the same height, one on each side: option (b).

questions.q: A square sheet is folded twice as shown (first left half onto right half, then top half onto bottom half) and a hole is punched. How will the sheet look when unfolded?
questions.solution:
Two folds → 4 layers → 4 holes.
Unfold fold 2 (horizontal line): the hole gets a partner reflected across the middle horizontal line, so the two holes are just below and just above the centre line on the right side.
Unfold fold 1 (vertical line): both holes get partners on the left side.
Result: 4 holes, two near the centre line on each side, the same distance from the middle line: option (c).

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution:
From the top corner there are 5 lines (2 sides + 3 inside lines).
They are cut by 2 horizontal lines (the base and the middle line).
Each triangle uses 2 corner lines and 1 horizontal line: C(5, 2) × 2 = 10 × 2 = 20.
